target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A superlative that ranks the part in a set of like parts or against a genus. This is the same as 'broadest' (C366) and 'smaller' (C243) in the previous review.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (2. continuum between two values; compound shape read by chain_from_phrase)
reason: A compound of two values, heart shaped (PATO_0000948) and ovate (FLOPO:0991024), with the degree word 'broadly'. Read it as a compound of these existing values; it needs no new term.
Horticultural word for tolerance of cold, drought or poor conditions, with no stated factor. It is vague and not a morphological quality of the plant.
'Pseudobulb monophyllous' and 'scape monophyllous' mean the part bears one leaf, so this is a count of leaves (1). The one-leaflet compound leaf is the separate term unifoliolate (FLOPO:0991073).
A compound of orbicular (PATO_0001934) and ovate (FLOPO:0991024): an ovate outline tending to round. Read it as a continuum of two existing values.

Long, slender, wand-like axes. Virgate already has 'wand-like' as a synonym. Whip-like stresses that the axes bend, so this mapping is approximate, and 'whip-like flower stalks' on an inflorescence should go to review.
It compares the fruit to a whole fruit type (small, dry, one-seeded, indehiscent), not to one quality. Annotate the qualities the source states, or the fruit type as bearer when the source gives it.

label: rose-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having an odour like that of roses. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991016 sweet-scented and FLOPO:0991017 spicy-scented, worded as they are.
reason: A specific, recurring scent in the same series as the existing FLOPO odour values. PATO has only the generic 'odorous'.

'Corolla stalk-like at base' and 'bract stalk-like below' describe a part narrowed at the base into a stalk-like part, which is the definition of clawed. Bare 'fruit stalk-like' and 'leaflet stalk-like in shape' are unclear and should stay unannotated.
Pulviniform means cushion-shaped. This follows the rule for 'cushion-shaped' (C315) in the previous review.
The part has no lenticels. This is the absence counterpart of 'lenticellate' (C204).
Persistent means not shed. 'Long' is a degree word and stays in the RDF record. The 'whole plant' statement (French source) probably refers to persistent leaves and needs review.
Every example says the stem has no roots arising at its nodes. This is not the negation of creeping (FLOPO:0991009), because a stem can lie on the ground without rooting.

The word has two meanings in the sources. On flowers it means papilionaceous (a pea-like flower); on fruits and galls (pisiform) it means small and globular, which pea-sized (FLOPO:0991041) and spherical (PATO_0001499) already cover. One rule cannot cover both meanings.
Maple-like leaves are palmately lobed. Leaf shape is the only reading the examples support.
A semi-shrub is a subshrub: woody only at the base. FLOPO already has the growth-form quality 'suffrutescent habit'. PO lists 'suffrutex' as a synonym of whole plant.
Virgate already has 'broom-like' as a related synonym. Limit the rule to whole plants: in the other examples 'brosses' (brushes) and 'witches' broom' (a gall disease) are not this quality.
'Depressed-globose' was mapped to oblate (C170). 'Sub-' makes the value approximate, so this is oblate with the approximate-value pattern.
It compares the fruit to a fig (a fruit type, the syconium) without naming a quality; 'capsule as fig' is a transcription fragment. No single shape or texture can be inferred.
It negates constricted. 'Centrally' is the region of the spathe, which the part-of-the-bearer slot handles.
A compound of undulate (PATO_0000967) and approximately crenate (scalloped, PATO_0001889, with the approximate-value pattern). The bearer 'wing' still needs the organ it belongs to.
'Sub-' with an existing value: shortly or almost stalked. This is the same treatment as 'suborbicular' in the approximate-value pattern.

label: gynaecandrous
definition: An androgynous quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its pistillate flowers being borne above the staminate flowers on the same axis. NOTE: Child of FLOPO:0991037 androgynous, whose definition does not fix the order. In Carex usage 'androgynous' means the opposite order (staminate above), which would need a sibling class.
reason: A standard sedge character (138 statements) whose meaning depends on the order of the flowers, which the existing androgynous class does not record.
French 'trigone' (achène trigone, ovaire trigone) means three-angled, which is trigonous.

target: new: quality of a borne part (stem has part leaf (PO_0025034) that is terete (PATO_0104016))
reason: 'Stems terete-foliate' (orchids) means the stems bear terete leaves. The quality belongs to the leaves, not the stem, so the annotation needs a has-part step rather than a stem term.

It means 'of two plates or lamellae' (a stigma with two flat lobes, a placenta with two plates), which is a count of parts. 'Lamella' has no PO class, so the count has no bearer yet and should go to review.

label: sexually reproducing
definition: A reproductive quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its producing seed or spores by meiosis and fertilization rather than asexually. NOTE: Contrasted in floras with apomictic or agamospermous plants, which would be a sibling class.
reason: 'Sexual or apomictic' records the breeding system of critical genera, and PATO has no term for the mode of reproduction.

label: spathe-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a spathe: a large bract enclosing or sheathing an inflorescence or flower, often split down one side. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002459 sepal-like, worded as they are.
reason: A common description of calyces and bracts (98 statements) in the same series as bract-like, petaloid and leaf-like.

label: spinose-serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's marginal teeth each ending in a spine. NOTE: Child of PATO:0001206 serrated. Numbers before it ('5-12-spinose-serrate on each side') are a count of teeth (docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md).
reason: It cannot be split into two values of the leaf, because the spine tips belong to the teeth (spine-tipped, FLOPO:0991210, describes the apex of the bearer). It is a common margin character (97 statements).

label: glume-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a glume (PO:0009039): small, dry, chaffy and bract-like. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002459 sepal-like, worded as they are.
reason: A recurring comparison in grass, sedge and rush descriptions (95 statements). The glume is a PO class, and this follows the earlier '-like' decisions.
